description: cctop — a btop-style live TUI that shows Claude Code internals (context, tokens, cost, limits, tools, agents, files, advisor) in a pane beside a running session. Rust + ratatui. Source PRD: tasks/prd-cctop.md v1.1.

userStories.title: Scaffold the Rust workspace and CI
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a buildable `cctop` binary with the core dependencies and CI so that every later story lands on a green base.
acceptanceCriteria: Cargo project `cctop` (edition 2021, Rust stable) with deps: ratatui, crossterm, tokio (rt-multi-thread, fs, time), notify, serde, serde_json, clap (derive), anyhow, thiserror, toml, insta (dev)

`cctop --version` prints the crate version; `cctop --help` lists subcommands `run` (default), `query`, `metrics`, `install`, `uninstall`, `hook`, `statusline-shim`, `split`, `advise`, `report`, `export` as stubs that exit 0 with `not implemented`
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs fmt check, clippy -D warnings, test on macOS and Ubuntu
`fixtures/` directory exists with a README explaining that fixture transcripts are anonymised copies of real `~/.claude/projects` files
Typecheck passes (`cargo check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
Tests pass (`cargo test`)

userStories.title: Session registry reader
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to parse `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` files so that cctop knows which Claude Code sessions exist.
acceptanceCriteria: `registry::Session` struct with fields pid, session_id, cwd, name, status (busy|idle|other), started_at, updated_at, version, kind, messaging_socket_path; unknown fields ignored
`registry::list(dir) -> Vec<Session>` reads every `*.json` in the directory; malformed files are skipped with a warning, not an error
`Session::is_alive()` checks the pid with `kill(pid, 0)` semantics (libc) and reports dead registry entries
Fixture: three registry files (busy, idle, dead pid) under `fixtures/sessions/`; tests cover all three
Typecheck passes (`cargo check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
Tests pass (`cargo test`)

userStories.title: Session discovery precedence
userStories.description: As a user, I want `cctop` with no arguments to attach to the session in my current terminal window so that I never copy a session id.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolution order: `--session <id|name|pid>` → `--cwd <path>` → tmux pane match (`tmux list-panes -F '#{pane_tty} #{pane_pid}'`, compare with the session pid's controlling TTY via `ps -o tty= -p`) → zellij (`$ZELLIJ` present: most recent busy session with cwd == $PWD) → most recently updated busy session with cwd == $PWD → error
`$CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` env var, when set, is used before all fallbacks except explicit `--session`
No session found: message `no Claude Code session found (try --session or --wait)` and exit code 2; `--wait` polls every 1 s until one appears
Unit tests for precedence with the fixture registry and injected env/tmux outputs (tmux call behind a trait so it can be mocked)
Typecheck passes (`cargo check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
Tests pass (`cargo test`)

userStories.title: Transcript line model
userStories.description: As a developer, I need typed, tolerant deserialisation of every transcript line kind so that parsing never fails on a new Claude Code version.
acceptanceCriteria: `transcript::Line` enum tagged on `type` with variants: User, Assistant, System (subtype: turn_duration, stop_hook_summary, away_summary, other), CostState, PermissionMode, QueueOperation, FileHistorySnapshot, Attachment, Unknown(raw)

Assistant lines expose message.id, model, effort, requestId, timestamp, content blocks (text, tool_use{id,name,input}, thinking), usage (input, cache_creation, cache_read, output, thinking_tokens, cache_creation.ephemeral_5m/1h, speed, service_tier)
User lines expose timestamp, content blocks (text, tool_result{tool_use_id, content, is_error}), toolUseResult (raw serde_json::Value), isMeta
CostState exposes totalCostUSD, totalAPIDuration, totalAPIDurationWithoutRetries, totalToolDuration, totalLinesAdded/Removed, modelUsage map

Fixture `fixtures/session-a.jsonl` (≥ 300 lines, anonymised real transcript containing a 13-block assistant response, a cost-state line, turn_duration and stop_hook_summary lines); test asserts every line parses to a non-Unknown variant except the ones expected to be Unknown
Typecheck passes (`cargo check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
Tests pass (`cargo test`)

userStories.title: Transcript tailer with live follow
userStories.description: As a user, I want new transcript lines reflected within 250 ms so that the dashboard is genuinely live.
acceptanceCriteria: `transcript::Tailer::open(path)` parses existing content from byte 0 and then follows appends using `notify` (kqueue/inotify) with a 1 s poll fallback
Partial trailing lines are buffered until `\n` arrives; file truncation/rotation restarts from 0; unknown line types are passed through as `Unknown`
Emits parsed lines on a tokio mpsc channel; a test appends 50 lines to a temp file after open and receives all 50 in order within 500 ms
Benchmark test (ignored by default): a 10 MB fixture parses in < 500 ms
Typecheck passes (`cargo check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
Tests pass (`cargo test`)

userStories.title: Usage aggregation with per-response deduplication and turn splitting
userStories.description: As a developer, I need token usage counted once per API response and grouped into turns so that every cost and context number is correct.
acceptanceCriteria: `metrics::Usage` accumulates input, cache_write_5m, cache_write_1h, cache_read, output, thinking; assistant lines sharing a `message.id` contribute once (first occurrence wins)

Turn boundaries: a turn starts at a non-meta user line whose content has no tool_result block and ends before the next such line; each turn records API call count (distinct message ids), usage, model(s), effort, start/end timestamps
Cache TTL per call derived from `cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens > 0` → 1h else 5m; session-level `observed_ttl` is the most recent
Context size per turn = cache_read + cache_creation + input of the turn's last API call
Test on the 13-block fixture asserts total output tokens equals the single response's count; test asserts turn count for session-a matches a hand-counted value
Typecheck passes (`cargo check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
Tests pass (`cargo test`)

userStories.title: Cost model with pricing table and cost-state calibration
userStories.description: As a user, I want cost figures that match Claude Code's own accounting so that I can trust the dollar amounts.
acceptanceCriteria: Bundled `pricing.toml` with per-model USD per MTok: input, cache_write_5m (1.25× input), cache_write_1h (2× input), cache_read (0.1× input), output; user override at `~/.config/cctop/pricing.toml` merged by model id
`metrics::Cost::estimate(usage, model)` uses the per-call TTL to choose the write price; unknown model → `None` (tokens only)

When a `cost-state` line exists, `Cost::authoritative` = totalCostUSD and per-model breakdown from modelUsage; `Cost::current()` = authoritative + estimate of calls newer than the cost-state line, flagged `approx: true` when any estimate contributes
Burn rate = cost over trailing 15 min × 4; tokens/min likewise; both computed from turn timestamps
Tests: estimate vs the fixture's cost-state total within 5 %; TTL price selection; unknown model
Typecheck passes (`cargo check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`)

userStories.title: Subagent transcript reader

userStories.title: Status-line shim and install/uninstall
userStories.description: As a user, I want cctop to see the status-line JSON so that context and rate limits are exact.
acceptanceCriteria: `cctop statusline-shim -- <original command...>` reads stdin, writes it atomically (temp + rename) to `~/.cctop/status/<sessionId>.json` (sessionId from the JSON's `session_id`), then execs the original command with the same stdin, passing stdout and exit code through; with no original command it prints nothing and exits 0; added latency < 3 ms measured in a test

`cctop install` backs up `~/.claude/settings.json` to `~/.cctop/backups/settings-<ts>.json`, rewrites `statusLine.command` to the shim form (idempotent), prints a unified diff and asks for confirmation unless `--yes`; `cctop uninstall` restores the original command

`status::watch(sessionId)` tails the file and exposes context_window (total_input_tokens, context_window_size), rate_limits (five_hour, seven_day: used_percentage, resets_at), model, plan, cost fields when present; retains a time series of (at, used_percentage) samples
